labrum

labrum, labrī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

lip

In this lexicon

  • lip

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 5.14: labrum superius; Plin. NH 9.64: īnferiōrī labrō; Traupman 58, 340

Notes

  1. 1labrum: short a (Lewis & Short lā̆brum, common). Hor. C. 1.13.12, dente labrīs notam, the close of a lesser asclepiad: la- takes a short place; Vergil makes the syllable heavy before br (E. 3.43, necdum illīs labra admōvī). De Vaan 319, s.v. labium. Lābrum, a basin, is another word, from lavābrum (de Vaan 330).

Examples

  • Torquātus volō parvulus mātris ē gremiō suae porrigēns tenerās manūs dulce rīdeat ad patrem sēmihiante labellō

    I want a little Torquatus, reaching out his tender hands from his mother’s lap, to laugh sweetly at his father with half-open lipsCatull. 61.209–213

    In the entry for lip

  • Platōnī cum in cūnīs parvulō dormientī apēs in labellīs cōnsēdissent

    when Plato was a baby asleep in his cradle and bees settled on his little lipsCic. Div. 1.78

    In the entry for lip

  • Domine, labia mea aperiēs, et ōs meum annūntiābit laudem tuam.

    Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.Vulg. Ps. 50 (51), 17
